one_month_reasoning: No Adobe-specific scheduled catalyst falls in the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30 window: Q3 FY26 was reported 2026-09-10, Q4 FY26 results come mid-December, Adobe MAX is 2026-11-10/12 (after the window) and the CEO handover is 2026-12-01. In-window drivers are peer software/mega-cap earnings in late October (sector read-through on AI monetization and seat pressure), the late-October FOMC and CFO-search headlines, all two-sided. The stock fell ~18% from its early-September high ($294) through the CEO announcement and a cautious Q4 guide; short-horizon reversal after a sharp drop and continued negative earnings-reaction momentum (five straight beats with a -5% average day-of reaction) roughly offset. So I centre almost exactly on today's price (median ~$238.5) with a ~10.5% one-month sigma (slightly under 41%/3.5 = 11.7% because no event is scheduled) plus a modest fat-tail mixture.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28E EPS ~$30.5 x 10x = $305, weight 0.5) and FCF yield (FY27E FCF/share ~$28 at a 9.5% yield = $295, weight 0.5), giving ~$300 twelve months out. This is a fundamental value; the market-price forecast median ($255) is lower because the base rate for AI-disruption-scare software is continued multiple pressure rather than quick re-rating.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus $27.67 grown ~10%: ~10-11% ARR growth (ARR +11.2%, FY26 ARR growth guide 10.2%) plus ~2-3% annual share-count shrink from buybacks (9.5M shares repurchased in Q3, $24.55B authorization left), minus some margin/pricing pressure.

Stock trades ~8.6x FY27 consensus today and ~13x forward per valueinvesting.io data (Intuit ~14x, Dropbox ~11.5x); forward P/E was 23-25x at start of 2024. I assume only a small re-rating from ~8.6x to 10x, consistent with Sparkline's finding that disruption-scare stocks median-return in line with the market rather than snapping back.

Current implied FCF yield ~10.5-11% at $238; I assume modest compression toward ~9.5%, still far above Adobe's historical 3-4% because the market treats AI-exposed software as a shrinking-surface-area asset (Swedroe/Sparkline value-trap framing).

bear.story: AI-native tools (Canva, Figma, Google, OpenAI) erode Creative Cloud seats and pricing; ARR growth slips toward 7-8%, new CEO resets FY27 guide at December earnings, more executive departures (open CFO search, Wadhwani exit), and a 35%-odds 2027 recession hits enterprise/Experience Cloud. Multiple slides to ~6.5x FY28 EPS of ~$26 = ~$170, below the June-2026 low of $190.

base.story: Adobe keeps printing ~10-11% ARR growth and ~12% EPS growth with heavy buybacks, AI-first ARR keeps compounding from $650M, but the market keeps it in the 'disruption scare' bucket; multiple stays ~8.5-9x NTM EPS of ~$30 => ~$255-265, a return in line with the market, matching the Sparkline base rate for such stocks.

bull.story: Chakravarthy's first guide (Dec-26) and MAX show credible freemium/agentic monetization, ARR re-accelerates to 12%+, and software keeps rallying from the 'SaaSpocalypse' bottom (IGV +40% off April lows). Multiple re-rates to ~12x FY28 EPS ~$30.5 = ~$365, similar to the 2022-23 rebound when ADBE rose ~85% in the year after its Sept-2022 Figma low.

thesis_break_reason: A close near $175 would be ~8% under the June-2026 panic low ($190.12) and ~6x forward EPS; with cash flow intact the stock has so far held above $190 even through the SaaSpocalypse, so trading there would most likely mean earnings power itself is breaking (ARR growth falling to mid-single digits, a guide-down under the new CEO, or evidence of net seat losses) rather than ordinary 41%-vol noise.

reasoning: Facts: Q3 FY26 (reported 2026-09-10) revenue $6.76B +13%, non-GAAP EPS $6.13, ARR $27.5B +11.2%, FY26 EPS guide raised to $24.45-24.50, Q4 guide below consensus; CEO succession to Anil Chakravarthy announced 2026-09-03 (stock -6.7% next day) with Wadhwani leaving and a CFO search open. At $238 the stock is ~9.7x FY26 and ~8.6x FY27 consensus EPS ($27.67), with net debt near zero and ~10-11% FCF yield; 39 analysts average $278 target, Hold. Base rates (my lane): (1) Sparkline's study of 'disruption scare' stocks (down 30%+ on tech-disruption fears; Adobe explicitly in the basket) finds median 12-month forward return about equal to the market, but interquartile range 1.8x wider, ~10% doubling and ~16% halving within a year. That argues for a median modestly above spot (market-like +7-8%) and fat tails both ways. (2) Adobe's own history: after the Sept-2022 Figma low (~$275) the stock rose ~85% in 12 months; but the 2024-2026 derating shows multiples can compress for years (forward P/E ~24x -> ~9x) while EPS grows ~12%/yr. (3) 2026 intra-year path: $190 June low to $293 in August and back to $238, consistent with ~41% realized vol. (4) Prediction markets: Polymarket ~35% US recession by end-2027 (2026-09-24, volume not shown on reachable page), a moderate macro headwind. Fundamental fair value ~$300 (P/E and FCF-yield blend) sits above my price median because the base rate for such names is that re-rating is slow; I set the 12-month median at ~$255 (EPS growth ~10-12% at a flat ~8.5-9x multiple) with effective lognormal sigma ~0.40 plus a fat-tail mixture, and scenario-weighted mean ~$264. P(>= spot) ~0.57. Limits: Alpha Vantage and Twelve Data estimate endpoints were unavailable (rate limit / plan), and some pages (Benzinga, predictionnews.com) returned 403, so the recession odds come from search-result snippets and consensus from stockanalysis.com.
